title: NOCTI Biotechnology 4275: Knowledge of Biotechnology - Biotechnology - Medical
subject: Biotechnology

questions.q: A patient diagnosed with HER2-positive breast cancer is prescribed the biopharmaceutical drug Trastuzumab (Herceptin). This drug specifically binds to the HER2 receptors on the surface of the cancer cells, flagging them for destruction by the immune system. What specific class of biotechnological therapeutic is Trastuzumab?
questions.explain:
Trastuzumab (and most therapeutics ending in the suffix **-mab**) is a **Monoclonal Antibody**. 

Monoclonal antibodies are highly specific proteins cloned and mass-produced in biomanufacturing facilities (typically using CHO cell lines). They are engineered to bind perfectly to one specific target antigen (like the HER2 receptor overexpressed on certain cancer cells), delivering highly targeted therapy without the systemic, wide-ranging toxicity of traditional chemical chemotherapy (small molecules).

questions.q: Prior to prescribing a standard dose of the blood-thinning drug Warfarin, a physician orders a microarray analysis of the patient's *CYP2C9* and *VKORC1* genes. The physician is using genetic information to predict how rapidly the patient's liver will metabolize the drug to prevent accidental overdose. This practice falls under which modern medical biotechnology sector?
questions.explain:
**Pharmacogenomics** is the study of how an individual's unique genetic makeup influences their physiological response to medications. 

Because different patients have different alleles for liver enzymes (like the Cytochrome P450 family), they process drugs at different speeds. By analyzing the genes beforehand, doctors can customize the dosage—moving away from "one-size-fits-all" medicine to precision medicine. 
> *Gene therapy* (Option 'a') actively alters the patient's DNA to cure disease.
